en: So what exactly are agent skills?
Agent skills are portable on-demand
capability packages, or skill packages is
really a good way of describing it, to
specialize your agent or to
just give your agent new skills. The name is
pretty fitting.
And the idea is that you have folders in
specific parts or in clearly defined
locations on your system to either set up a
global skill skill or a project-specific
local skill.
And in those folders, you have at least a
skill.md file, which is simply a markdown
file, which in the end contains a prompt.
You could say it contains text that is
injected into a session, into a chat session
you have with your agent to give that agent
extra context, extra information, extra
instructions depending on what your skill is
about. And we'll see examples over the next
lectures, no worries.
In addition to that mandatory skill MD file,
your skill can also come with other features
like, for example, scripts that belong to
the skill so that the agent has something to
execute if your skill needs that, extra
references, which are extra markdown files
with more information the agent can use to
dive deeper, and potentially extra assets
like HTML templates or anything like that.
And again, we'll see skills in practice in
just a second. But the idea behind skills is
that really you can use them to inject extra
knowledge, extra expertise into a session,
or to define repeatable workflows. So
instructions you otherwise send to the agent
over and over again, by putting them into a
skill, you just have to make sure that this
skill gets activated by the agent. And that
in turn is something which the agent should
normally do automatically if the skill is
properly set up, since the idea behind these
agent skills is that agents can discover and
activate them,
load that extra information into the session
automatically, though you can also
explicitly invoke skills, as you'll see.
And this entire skills feature is
standardized, as mentioned. You can, for
example, also use agent skills with Claude
Code, with Codex, and with other coding
agents. But
let's simply dive in, shall we?
